chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mu'addab (RA) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abu Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari narrated to me, saying: I said to Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (AS)

O son of the Messenger of Allah! What do you say about the Qur'an, for there has been a dispute among us regarding it? Some people said: 'It is created,' and some people said: 'It is not created.' He (AS) replied: 'As for me, I do not say what they say, but I say: It is the Word of Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What is Imam Musa ibn Ja'far's view on whether the Qur'an is created or uncreated?
ai.summary: Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (AS) navigates the early theological controversy between the Mu'tazilites (who argued the Qur'an was created) and the Hanbalis/Atharis (who argued it was uncreated) by affirming it as the 'Speech of Allah' (Kalam Allah). This position aligns with the Shia scholarly tradition of avoiding extreme anthropomorphism or temporalization, emphasizing the Qur'an as an eternal attribute of God's essence rather than a separate created entity. By using the term 'Kalam,' the Imam preserves the divine origin and authority of the text without entering the metaphysical specifics of 'creation' (khalq) versus 'non-creation' (la khalq).
